newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT to invest in Y2.7 bln Malaysia project.
newsitem.headline: NTT to invest in Y2.7 bln Malaysia project.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp said on Wednesday that it had formed a joint venture in Malaysia with several Malaysian companies to push the country's multibillion dollar "cybercity" project.
NTT took a 15 percent stake in the new company, called Cyberview, for 51.2 million ringgit, or about 2.7 billion yen, NTT president Junichiro Miyazu told a news conference.

Cyberview will develop a new high-technology industrial region, modelled after California's Silicon Valley and featuring advanced transportation and telecommunications infrastructure, on a 7,000-hectare site near Kuala Lumpur.
Miyazu said NTT had been selected as the major contractor in the Malaysian government's project and would send managers and workers to work with Cyberview.
Miyazu said the investment was part of NTT's plan to become a multimedia service provider.
"It's a step forward as NTT transforms itself into a multimedia service company from a telephone wiring company," Miyazu told the news conference.
NTT would also establish a subsidiary and a research and development centre in the new city, called Cyberjava, by September this year, Miyazu said.
He added that NTT had been granted a special designation by the Malaysian government giving it preferential tax treatment and exempting it from rules limiting the employment of foreigners.
